Leon shared that he has seen EasyPay approve customers with very low credit scores and has a good understanding of how the program works. However, he noted that he is sometimes hesitant to heavily promote financing due to the number of customer declines. He also mentioned that some customers who receive pre-approvals become uncomfortable when asked to provide their full banking information, expressing concerns about privacy, security, and potential fraud. As a result, some customers choose not to complete the application process.

Despite these challenges, Leon stated that he continues to promote EasyPay and plans to keep offering it as a financing solution. At this time, he reported no questions or concerns.

Subject: 00TTO00000zSvBU2A0
Full Comments:
Spoke with Mike and assisted him with logging into the new platform successfully.

During our conversation, I asked about his current financing usage. Although he has been enrolled with EasyPay for quite some time, he shared that they have had very little to no usage over the years. I asked whether this was due to having other financing options or if customers simply were not interested in financing. Mike explained that the majority of their customer base is from a well-established, higher-income community, so most customers pay out of pocket and rarely need financing.

I informed him that I set up a $20 SPIF for every fully funded EasyPay application. Francisco showed me their customer workflow through Tech Metric, where they have integrated the EasyPay application link into their inspection and estimate process. After completing a vehicle inspection, customers receive an electronic report with inspection details and the repair estimate, and the EasyPay application link is included at the bottom of every estimate sent. This ensures financing is presented to all customers as part of their standard process. While adoption may be limited due to the area’s customer demographics and lower financing demand, it was encouraging to see EasyPay incorporated into their customer communication process.

Subject: 00UTO00000cRwzi2AC
Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Spoke with Sabrina, the manager. After several months of follow-up visits encouraging the shop to use EasyPay again, they are finally back on board and are now running EasyPay first. They are once again producing the same level of business they did with us when we were RIC, which is a great win.

This is a good example of how consistent relationship-building and periodic follow-up can help re-engage inactive merchants over time.

Sabrina shared that overall business has been slower, but higher repair costs have resulted in larger average ticket sizes, helping offset the decrease in car count. Based on their current activity, I estimate they have the potential to fund approximately $8K–$10K with EasyPay each month.

The shop is currently on a $20 spiff. Sabrina requested a poster, which I will provide once they are back in stock. I reminded her to reach out to Connor or me if she needs any assistance.

Help your customers get EasyPay texts again
 

 



If a customer stopped EasyPay texts, they can text START to 619-327-9835 to start getting them again.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Help Your Customers Get Our Texts Again
 
 
 
 Hello, 
 Text messaging runs through a long chain of carriers, apps, and filtering systems, and more of them are applying automated opt-outs on a customer’s behalf without notifying the sender.
 If a customer ever replied STOP, blocked our number, or was opted out automatically, they stop getting EasyPay texts – including the application link you send at the counter. Getting them reconnected takes one quick text.
 
 
 
 To Reconnect, Just Text
 START
 to
 619-327-9835
 One text and they’re reconnected right away – no forms, no calls, no waiting.
 
 
 
 How you can help:
 

 
 
 
 ✓

Subject: 00UTO00000dFFRh2AO
Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
I spoke with Tre, the manager. He said he really likes the program and has made EasyPay his go-to financing vendor. He prefers EasyPay over KOALAFI because we do not require him to separate parts and labor on repair orders. He explained that he only uses KOALAFI when EasyPay does not approve enough to cover the full repair.

Tre mentioned that he has had some issues in the past regarding sales tax on invoices. Connor previously reviewed the proper procedures with him. He asked me how the tax exemption works and whether the shop could get in trouble for not charging sales tax. I showed him the Georgia reseller tax ID number located in his Business Center and advised him to have the owner provide that number to their tax professional, who would know how to handle it appropriately.

Tre had no other questions or concerns. I left behind a few EasyPay pens and notepads and reminded him to reach out to Connor or me if he ever needs assistance.

Robert provided two recent examples that have been frustrating for both him and his customers. One customer had previously completed a lease with EasyPay but was declined when applying again. Another customer was initially approved, but after the approval expired and they reapplied, the second application was denied.

Robert expressed frustration with these situations because EasyPay is their only financing solution for customers who cannot pay the full repair cost upfront. I acknowledged his concerns, thanked him for the feedback, and encouraged him to continue reaching out whenever he encounters situations where we may be able to assist.

I recommended that they consider running EasyPay first, as the program tends to perform best when it is presented before receiving declines from other financing providers. Jeff appreciated the feedback and thanked me for the suggestion.

I sent over my contact information and encouraged him to reach out if any questions or concerns come up.

Subject: 00UTO00000dC8Ht2AK
Full Comments:
I spoke with Brad, the manager. He told me that although business has been up and down for the past several months, this month has been much better. He believes the increase is due to customers getting their vehicles ready for back-to-school season.

EasyPay remains their go-to financing option. His only concern was the approval rate. We reviewed his dashboard and found that they had submitted eight applications, with two approvals. The positive takeaway is that they funded both approved applications, giving them an excellent pull-through rate.

I explained what I’ve been telling other shops: in the current economy, many customers are falling behind on payments, which negatively impacts their credit profiles and results in more financing declines. He understood and had no additional questions or concerns. I reminded him to reach out to Connor or me if he needs anything.

Full Comments:
Spoke with Ricardo, the owner, to discuss how business has been and how EasyPay has been supporting their sales. Ricardo shared that business has been very slow, as they are a two-man shop currently servicing only 2–3 vehicles per week.

Their average repair order ranges from $6,000 to $10,000, and most customers pay using multiple personal credit cards because financing options, including EasyPay, typically do not provide enough approval amount to cover the full repair. Ricardo also mentioned they offer Snap Finance, but only process about 1–2 applications per month due to the same limitation.

Overall, Ricardo explained that low customer volume, high repair costs that exceed available financing limits, and a lack of a strong financing culture among their customer base have all contributed to minimal finance utilization.

Subject: 00UTO00000dTite2AC
Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Here’s a polished Salesforce note:

Spoke with Lewis, the owner of Mission Motorsports. He expressed frustration with the new portal, explaining that some EasyPay contract notifications are being filtered as spam, preventing customers from receiving and signing their contracts. As a result, they’ve lost financing opportunities because customers were unable to complete the process.

Lewis pointed to a customer in the waiting area as a recent example. The customer was unable to receive the EasyPay contract, ultimately financed through Snap instead, and completed the transaction without any issues.

I provided Lewis with my direct phone number and asked him to contact me immediately if this happens again so I can help resolve it. I also explained that contracts can be resent from the 619 number as a workaround. This is a significant pain point for the merchant and is impacting their confidence in using EasyPay.

This account appears to have strong potential if we can continue building preference for EasyPay despite the corporate first-look process. James is a good advocate for our program, so maintaining a strong relationship with him will be important.

Full Comments:
Completed onboarding with Chris. He had very few questions throughout the session and found the EasyPay process to be straightforward.

During the onboarding, we reviewed key requirements and best practices, including properly itemizing invoices, the tax exemption process, and ensuring that no taxes are included on EasyPay invoices. I also showed him the Texas tax exemption document and explained when and how it should be used.

We discussed the requirement that all EasyPay transactions must be completed in person and reviewed the importance of verifying that the customer's government-issued ID matches the information submitted on the application.

Chris shared that he is already familiar with similar financing processes, as they currently work with Synchrony, Kafene, American First, and Snap Finance. Overall, he had no significant questions or concerns and felt the process was clear and easy to follow.

During the onboarding, we reviewed key requirements and best practices, including properly itemizing invoices, the tax exemption process, and ensuring that no taxes are included on EasyPay invoices. I also showed him the Texas tax exemption document and explained when and how it should be used.

We discussed the requirement that all EasyPay transactions must be completed in person and reviewed the importance of verifying that the customer's government-issued ID matches the information submitted on the application.

Chris shared that he is already familiar with similar financing processes, as they currently work with Synchrony, Kafene, American First, and Snap Finance. Overall, he had no significant questions or concerns and felt the process was clear and easy to follow.
